hook: "this slideshow account is literally leaving money on the table, it's almost infuriating"
body: A case study of a slideshow account going viral "on basically every second post" where the format itself shows the app and primes the download — the frustration being that the owner isn't monetizing the attention.
cta: none visible (link to the example video).
idea: Slideshows that demo the product inside the slides are self-priming funnels — virality without monetization is the missed opportunity.
sequencing: Hook: an account "leaving money on the table."
Proof: going viral on basically every second post.
Mechanism: the format already shows the app and primes download.
Frustration: the owner isn't capturing it.
formatting: Short text + 31s video showing the slideshow format in action.
why_it_works: The "infuriating" framing makes the reader feel smarter than the account owner, which earns the share — and the real payload is the format observation.
what_to_steal: The format-as-funnel insight for LC: design slideshows where each slide IS the product demo (stacking, waterproof tests), so the content primes the purchase without a hard pitch.

hook: "these are the types of outsized organic views you get on new accounts when you nail"
body: A case study of outsized organic views on new slideshow accounts: nail the target audience ("pinterest aesthetic girlies"), have one visually viral feature (image overlay), and cast the right UGC creator.
idea: Three levers drive slideshow virality: exact audience understanding, one visually viral feature, and the right creator face.
sequencing: Hook: outsized organic views on NEW accounts.
Lever 1: audience understanding (= pinterest aesthetic girlies).
Lever 2: one visually viral feature (image overlay).
Lever 3: the right UGC creator.
Proof: attached media.
formatting: Short text + photo + 9s video. Three-bullet success formula.
why_it_works: Reducing virality to three checkable levers makes it feel replicable rather than lucky, which is what operators will pay attention to.
what_to_steal: The three-lever formula as LC's slideshow brief template: name the aesthetic tribe, pick ONE visual signature (e.g., wrist-stack overlays), cast one face per account.

hook: "this guy just proved slideshows convert way harder than videos 😭"
body: A case study of a new account that found a viral slideshow format, built an app to fit it, and spammed it — arguing slideshows convert harder than video because they're easy to make, cheap to scale, and algo-pushed. Claims $10k MRR is easier than people think once the format is found.
cta: none visible (quoted post links an X article with "the real numbers").
idea: Don't fit your product to a format — find a viral slideshow format first, then build the offer to fit it.
sequencing: Hook: slideshows convert harder than videos.
Why: easy to make, cheap to scale, algo-pushed.
Thesis: $10k MRR is easier than you think.
Method: find a viral replicable format → build the app to fit → spam it.
Proof: the quoted article's real numbers.
formatting: Hype thread + quoted X article; two photos. Exclamatory, informal.
why_it_works: "Convert harder than videos" is a contrarian claim with a simple mechanism list, and the format-first inversion gives builders a concrete starting point.
what_to_steal: The reversed workflow for LC: instead of making jewelry content, find the viral jewelry slideshow format first (aesthetic stack carousels, "rate my stack"), then pour LC product into it at volume.

body: A first-person proof post: one slideshow account started last month, 1M+ views on slideshows alone, 10,000 app downloads. Pure receipt.
idea: One slideshow account can drive 1M views and 10k downloads in a month — the format is a distribution channel, not a content type.
sequencing: Setup: started the account last month.
Views: 1M+ on slideshows.
Outcome: 10,000 downloads.
Kicker: "One slideshow account."
why_it_works: Extreme brevity + two hard numbers; the post is 90% receipt, which is why it travels.
what_to_steal: The benchmark for LC's own slideshow farm: one account, one month, 1M views → set that as the target and staff accordingly.

hook: "You swiped through that slideshow 3 times today."
body: A replication tutorial: find a slideshow account to copy, study its formats and views, then paste the slides into ChatGPT Astra and ask it to reverse-engineer why they work. The video breaks down the hook at 0:25.
cta: none visible (two video links showing the method).
idea: Slideshow virality is reverse-engineerable: feed the slides to an AI and have it decode the hook mechanics, then replicate.
sequencing: Hook: "You swiped through that slideshow 3 times today."
Demystify: nobody filmed or edited it.
Tease: "Watch until 0:25" for the hook breakdown.
Method: find account → study formats/views → paste slides into Astra → ask why.
Implied CTA: go replicate.
formatting: Short instructional text + 30s video. Direct second-person voice.
why_it_works: The opening line implicates the reader (you did swipe 3 times), which proves the format's grip before the tutorial even starts.
what_to_steal: The exact SOP for LC's slideshow program: pick 5 viral jewelry slideshow accounts, feed their slides to an LLM for hook decoding, and templatize the winners before producing a single slide.

hook: "bro is doing $9k a month with a single tiktok slideshow account 😭"
body: A case study: one person doing $9k/month from a single TikTok slideshow account. The playbook: build an app that fits a format, exploit that format across 10 accounts, and the snowball compounds toward $100k.
idea: The slideshow arbitrage: one format × 10 accounts = a compounding revenue snowball.
sequencing: Hook: $9k/mo, one slideshow account.
Wake-up call framing.
Playbook: build an app that fits a format.
Scale: exploit across 10 accounts → $100k.
Snowball: it only gets bigger.
formatting: Short hype post + screenshot photo. Wake-up-call tone.
why_it_works: $9k from "a single account" makes the unit economics feel trivially copyable, and the 10-account extrapolation turns a case study into a plan.
what_to_steal: The multi-account math for LC: don't run one slideshow account — run 10 persona-varied accounts (gym girl, office, beach, bride) on the same jewelry slideshow template and let the winners compound.

product: commentary — no product (hiring post for a faith-and-focus app)
hook: "Hiring creators for a faith and focus app"
body: A hiring post: recruiting creators for a faith-and-focus app at $200/mo trial (rising with performance) to make faceless slideshows — explicitly requiring applicants who have already grown a slideshow account.
cta: Comment "BIBLE" + follow to apply; send your best carousels.
idea: Slideshow growth is now a hireable skill: pay proven slideshow-account growers a trial rate to run your faceless funnel.
sequencing: Role: creators for a faith and focus app.
Pay: $200/mo trial, rises on performance.
Format: faceless slideshows, no filming.
Requirement: must have grown a slideshow account.
Application: send best carousels, comment "BIBLE" + follow.
formatting: Short classified-style hiring post. Bullet requirements.
why_it_works: It prices the skill honestly ($200 trial) while the "must have grown one" filter does the quality control the interview can't.
what_to_steal: The hiring filter for LC's slideshow farm: only hire creators who have already grown a slideshow account — proof of the skill, not promises — and pay trial-then-performance.

hook: "Imagine your AI agent posting 1000s of viral TikTok slideshows like this, every single day 🤯"
body: A 7-step playbook for an AI agent posting thousands of viral TikTok slideshows daily: rent US iPhones (Minionix), create persona accounts, warm them in-niche, generate slideshows from a 100K Pinterest image DB, schedule posts, and have the agent double down on winners. Claims persona accounts with the same caption hit 7.6M-34.6M views. Flagged in-file as a ToS risk (account farming).
idea: Slideshow distribution can be fully agent-operated: 100 accounts × 1 post/day = 3,000 slideshows/month driving traffic to one product.
sequencing: Vision: AI agent posting 1000s of slideshows daily.
Steps 1-3: rent US iPhones, create persona accounts, warm in-niche.
Steps 4-5: generate from 100K Pinterest DB, schedule.
Step 6: agent checks performance daily, makes more winners.
Math: 100 accounts/day = 3,000/month → all to your product.
formatting: Numbered 7-step playbook post; screenshots of persona accounts with view counts.
why_it_works: The math (3,000/month) makes the scale feel mechanical and inevitable, which is catnip for operators — while the ToS risk is the part to leave behind.
what_to_steal: The closed-loop mechanic (agent reviews daily performance and produces more of what wins) — LC can run this loop on its legitimate creator accounts without the rented-phone farm the post also describes.
